result.summary: Reviewed git diff main...HEAD (lib/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation.ex new, lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex + lib/letflow/definitions.ex modified) against the four reviewer questions, docs/anti-patterns.md, and the design doc (lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md). (1) Idiomatic vs crutch: SemanticValidation.validate/2 is a pure function (no Repo/Ecto/Logger/clock/IO), same shape as the existing sibling delegate modules SubProcessInterface/FormSchemaExpressions -- a genuine pattern reuse, not a new abstraction invented ahead of need. No GenServer-doing-a-state-machine's-job pattern anywhere; this is validation logic, not a process. (2) Supervision: confirmed zero diff to lib/letflow/instance_supervisor.ex or lib/letflow/*/process_instance.ex -- this requirement never touches process supervision, consistent with REQ-045's process-vs-row decision; nothing here collapses isolation. (3) Type-safety: hd(path) on {:var, path} is safe by construction (Expr's parser never emits an empty path -- already verified independently by SECURITY-REVIEWER's INV-8 check in step-02c); the type_family()/operand_family() sentinel scheme (:null_literal, :unresolvable, :unknown) is a reasonable, well-contained internal representation -- no invalid-state class here that a struct/Ecto.Enum change would make meaningfully safer, so no docs/issues/ filing warranted for this module. (4) Scope creep: none found -- the module implements exactly AC1-AC7, defers OQ-1..OQ-6 (nested-path resolution, arithmetic/builtin operand typing, multi-type-family fields, structural-check wiring into activate/2) explicitly rather than building speculative machinery for them; this is scope discipline, not creep. Levenshtein: verified by direct read (lines 174-202) -- real iterative Wagner-Fischer DP over String.graphemes/1 with a proper prev-row/this-row fold, not a stub or first-alphabetical fallback; manually traced levenshtein_distance('cusotmer_name','customer_name') == 2 matches ELIXIR-DEV's own reported sanity check. Moduledoc (lines 56-91, 93-110): the full 5x5 comparable/non-comparable type-pair table is stated explicitly in a literal markdown table plus prose restatement (not left inferential), and the HUMAN_TASK-routing-out-of-scope decision is stated explicitly with its grep-verified reasoning (no HUMAN_TASK-to-Expr routing mechanism exists in lib/letflow/ today) -- both match the handoff's specific scrutiny points verbatim. create/2 + update/2 divergence: confirmed by direct grep (create/2 at line 547, update/2 at line 1635, validate_update_graph/1 at line 1664) -- none of these are touched by the diff; only validate_definition_graph/2 (line ~1253) and the new run_semantic_validation/2 helper wired into activate/2 (line ~2313) gate on the new pass, exactly as the design's own §3.1 states and flags for REVIEWER. ENDORSING this as a genuine behavioral choice, not a silent gap: the design's justification is grounded directly in the requirement's own source UAT scenario (definition-type-error-blocked.yaml) and EO-001/EO-002's 'fix one problem at a time, draft stays saveable' semantics, is explicitly flagged rather than quietly decided, and does not contradict any docs/migration/decisions/ record -- REQ-288's own create/2+update/2 strictness was for CEL-grammar validity specifically (a different, narrower guarantee), not a blanket precedent that every future check must also block draft-save. Confirmed zero diff to lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex and zero diff under web/ (git diff --stat main...HEAD). mix compile --warnings-as-errors exits 0 (re-ran independently). No entries in docs/anti-patterns.md were violated. Non-blocking note for the record (not a defect): field_existence_violations/3 and type_compatibility_violations/3 each walk the same parsed ast() independently (collect_var_paths/1 and collect_cmp_nodes/1 are two separate full traversals per edge) rather than a single combined walk -- harmless at this AST size and a deliberate simplicity/readability tradeoff, but worth a second look if edge conditions grow materially larger.
